text.p: OMAHA, Neb., June 10 (Reuter) Northern Border Pipeline Co said its Chicago Project received a Final Environmental Impact Statement from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission staff showing steps needed to receive approval of the project.

In the statement, the FERC staff concluded that approval of the proposed project, with the recommended mitigating measures, would have limited environmental impact and would be an environmentally acceptable action, the pipeline said.
All mitigative measures required by the statement are being incorporated into Northern Border Pipeline's construction plan for the Chicago Project, it said.

"We believe that the favorable (environmental statement) clears the way for the FERC to issue a final certificate affirming the economic and regulatory findings in the preliminary determination issued in August 1996," Northern Border's statement continued

"We are confident that with this finding, our solid market demonstration, and our strong base of customer support that the FERC will promptly issue final approval of the Chicago Project. Separately, debt financing for the Chicago Project has been arranged and is expected to close next week," it concluded.

The Chicago Project would increase the pipeline's natural gas receipt capabilities to 2.4 billion cubic feet per day from the existing 1.7 billion daily and allow for additional deliveries of 1.2 billion cubic feet per day into the Chicago area.
Northern Border said the Chicago Project is estimated to cost $837 million and is targeted for a November 1, 1998, in-service date.
Northern Border Pipeline is a general partnership which owns and operates a 969-mile interstate pipeline that transports about 20 percent of all Canadian gas imported into the United States.

Northern Border Partners LP owns a 70 percent general partner interest in Northern Border Pipeline. The remaining 30 percent interest in Northern Border Pipeline is owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd.
